title: Positivity of the Threshold
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function. Write $T(f)$ for the sum, over the $n$ coordinates, of the expected squared discrete derivatives of $f$, and set $\rho(\eta)=\eta/(2+\eta)$ and $\Theta(f,\epsilon,\eta,k)=(\frac{\epsilon}{T(f)}\rho(\eta)^k)^{1+\eta}$. If $\epsilon>0$, $\eta>0$, $k$ is a natural number, and $T(f)>0$, then $\Theta(f,\epsilon,\eta,k)>0$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
